title: Open the next release: `$schema` stamps name the format's shape

ground.note: The brief: both decisions of 2026-10-08, their motive, what the spec must cover, the constraints.

Where this sits: first of the three steps toward guarantee-reports. Also the provider-answer decision of 2026-10-08: older shapes are refused by name before 1.0, and read through their frozen shape and lifted after it.
The release process as documented today: the cut's steps, the rehearsal, the workflow's version check and the docs deploy.
Cut, regenerate the usage spec and CLI docs, test, commit, tag, push. --rehearse stops before committing.

Requires a version newer than package.json's and a ledger ending at package.json's version. Bumps three manifests, renames next snapshots, regenerates, appends to the ledger, and rewrites the hello-world stamps.
Cut on a copy: manifests, snapshots, ledger, and the refusals that write nothing.
The tag-triggered workflow. It checks that npm/package.json and packages/schemas/package.json equal the tag, then deploys the docs site, stage-publishes both packages and creates the GitHub release.
Its last step rehearses a cut of package.json's next patch (PR #127).
Static invariants on release.yml, docs-deploy.yml, ci.yml and release.sh.

defineFormat. It refuses a stamp newer than the package and one below FIRST_SUPPORTED_RELEASE. A stamp at its own version tries next first and then falls back to the latest released shape at or below the stamp.
PACKAGE_VERSION 0.20.0, FIRST_SUPPORTED_RELEASE 0.17.0, CURRENT_SHAPES (each format's last-changed release, or next).
Release ledger 0.17.0 … 0.20.0; the docs site serves schemas for these releases.
The bridge. withSchemaUrl stamps PHAX_RELEASE. readCurrent refuses a stamp newer than PHAX_RELEASE. The answer readers accept a stamp newer than 0.19.0, or one equal to the running release.
Generated PHAX_RELEASE: what --version prints and every document is stamped with.
DIAGNOSTICS_EXPECTED_SHAPE names gate-diagnostics at PHAX_RELEASE in the missing-document hint.
Generates and checks the package's generated index and src/schemas/release.ts from package.json and the snapshots.
Expects the ledger to end at package.json's version; checkLedger reports a mismatch.
Prints gate-diagnostics/0.20.0; the cut rewrites it today. brief.mjs prints brief-answer/0.20.0 the same way.
Extend phax: the stamped examples, and the sentence saying `$schema` names the release the document is written for.

Q16 q-release-name: `$schema` names the root package.json version, and an unreleased shape is the `next` snapshot release.sh renames. Q20 q-support-start: support starts at the first release that writes `$schema`.

problem:
Both flaws are in what a stamp names.

First, a stamp names the running release, not the shape. Every document carries the release that wrote it, and the package refuses a release newer than its own version. A consumer on @lbdremy/phax-schemas 0.20 therefore cannot read a `phase-status` that phax 0.21 writes, even when `phase-status` did not change. Providers hit the same wall: steme pins phax's request URLs as constants, so it breaks at every release. Every consumer must upgrade at every phax release, whether or not a format it reads changed.

Second, during a development cycle one stamp names two shapes. While the manifests name the last release, say 0.19.0, a development build stamps 0.19.0 on documents in the shape in progress, and the released 0.19.0 stamped the same number on the old shape. Everything that copes with this changes meaning at the cut:
- the package's fallback from `next` to the latest released shape exists only before a cut;
- the answer readers' exception for the running release reads that release as `next`;
- tests written mid-cycle stamped `PACKAGE_VERSION` and relied on the fallback. They broke the 0.20.0 release gate (fixed in e79dcdd7), and 0.19.0's gate had failed the same way.

Providers are exposed too. A provider answering in the cycle's new answer shape has to stamp 0.19.0, and the installed 0.19.0 then reads it with the old shape, silently, where it should refuse it as newer. PR #127 catches the tests at review time, but the ambiguity they rely on remains.

productGoal.guidingRule: A $schema stamp names a format's shape, never the build that wrote it, and no two shapes ever share a stamp.

terminology.definition: The X.Y.Z in a document's `$schema` URL.
The stamp phax writes for a format. It is the release named by the format's latest release-named snapshot or, while the format has a `next` snapshot, the opened version.
The unreleased X.Y.Z that the three manifests name between one release and the next cut. No released build writes it, and no released document carries it.
The commit that sets the three manifests, and the files generated from them, to an opened version. It happens right after each release, or by hand to change the opened version (a re-opening).
What `scripts/release-cut.ts` does for a release: it names the opened version's shapes (renames `next` snapshots) and records the opened version in the ledger.
The release ledger's last entry: the newest version ever cut.
phax or the schemas package built from a commit whose manifests name an opened version.
The version a reader compares stamps against: phax's `PHAX_RELEASE`, or the package's own version. It is a release in a release build and the opened version in a development build.
A stamp below its format's current stamp. Example: gate-diagnostics 0.20.0 while an unreleased gate-diagnostics change is opened as 0.21.0.

requirements.title: Writers stamp the shape
requirements.statement: phax shall stamp every document it writes with that format's current stamp, not with its running version. This covers each persisted file, each request it hands a gate step or brief provider, and the expected-document hint.

requirements.title: phax's stamps agree with the snapshots
requirements.statement: IF phax's current stamp for any format differs from the one the committed snapshots and the manifests' version record THEN the schemas check shall fail and name the format.

requirements.title: Newer refusal compares the running version
requirements.statement: IF a document's stamp is newer than the reader's running version THEN the reader shall refuse it as newer and name both versions. phax applies this to persisted files and answers; the package applies it to every format.

requirements.title: An unchanged format stays readable
requirements.statement: WHEN a reader meets a document of a format unchanged since release S, stamped with any version from S up to the reader's running version, THE reader SHALL read it as that format's current shape.

requirements.title: The package reads an opened stamp by next alone
requirements.statement: WHILE a format's current shape is the unreleased `next`, THE schemas package SHALL read a document stamped with the package's own version by `next` alone. When `next` rejects it, the package SHALL report `next`'s violation and never fall back to a released shape.

requirements.title: Answers are read in the current shape only
requirements.statement: phax shall read a gate step's diagnostics document or a brief provider's answer only when its stamp is at or above the format's current stamp and at or below phax's running version. The running version gets no exception of its own.

requirements.title: Older-shape answers are refused by name
requirements.statement: IF an answer's stamp is below its format's current stamp THEN phax shall refuse it as an older shape, by name, and name the `$schema` URL it reads. A stamp at or below the last release that lacked the answer format (0.19.0) keeps its existing refusal.

requirements.title: phax names the stamp it reads
requirements.statement: WHEN phax refuses a diagnostics document or brief answer, or reports one missing, THE system SHALL name the `$schema` URL of that format's current stamp.

requirements.title: A development build reads the installed release's files
requirements.statement: WHILE phax is a development build, THE system SHALL read every file the installed release wrote exactly as that release reads it.

requirements.title: A release refuses a development build's opened stamp
requirements.statement: IF a released phax or a released schemas package reads a document stamped with a version opened after it THEN it shall refuse the document as newer.

requirements.title: The development-build refusal is unchanged
requirements.statement: The first supported release shall stay the lowest release-named snapshot. The development-build refusal shall apply only to stamps below it, so an opened version never meets it.

requirements.title: release.sh opens the next minor
requirements.statement: WHEN release.sh has pushed the tag of release X.Y.Z THE script SHALL commit and push an opening of X.(Y+1).0. The three manifests, the generated version mirrors, the usage spec and the CLI reference name the new version; the ledger and the snapshots are untouched.

requirements.title: Opening by hand
requirements.statement: WHEN the operator runs `scripts/release.sh --open <X.Y.Z>` on a clean tree THE script SHALL commit an opening of that version. It SHALL refuse a version that is not X.Y.Z, is not newer than the last release, or equals the version the manifests already name.

requirements.title: A failed opening says how to finish
requirements.statement: IF the opening fails after the release tag is pushed THEN release.sh shall exit non-zero and print the `--open` command that completes it.

requirements.title: Only the opened version is cut
requirements.statement: IF the version given to the cut is not the opened version the manifests name THEN the cut shall refuse before writing anything. The refusal SHALL name the opened version and the `--open` command that re-opens to the requested one.

requirements.title: The ledger gains a release at its cut
requirements.statement: WHEN the cut runs THE cut SHALL require the opened version to be newer than the ledger's last entry, and SHALL append it to the ledger in the release commit.

requirements.title: The cut changes no stamp
requirements.statement: The cut shall rename every `next` snapshot to the opened version. It shall change no manifest version, no stamp a development build writes and no stamp an example prints.

requirements.title: Example stamps follow the shape
requirements.statement: IF the stamp a hello-world script prints (audit.mjs's gate-diagnostics, brief.mjs's brief-answer) differs from its format's current stamp THEN a test shall fail and name the script.

requirements.title: Only cut releases are listed and served
requirements.statement: The ledger and the docs site shall list and serve only versions that were cut. The site build shall accept a ledger whose last entry is at or below package.json's version, and refuse one that lists a version above it.

requirements.title: A tag needs a cut
requirements.statement: IF a pushed tag's commit holds a ledger whose last entry is not the tag's version THEN the release workflow shall fail before it deploys the site or stages a package.

requirements.title: What a development build reports
requirements.statement: WHILE phax is a development build, `phax --version`, `phax.usage.kdl` and `docs/cli/reference.md` SHALL report the opened version as a bare X.Y.Z.

requirements.title: CI rehearses the opened version
requirements.statement: CI shall rehearse a cut of the opened version the manifests name, not of a version computed from it.

requirements.title: The first opened cycle
requirements.statement: WHEN this change lands on main THE repository SHALL be opened at 0.21.0, with the ledger still ending at 0.20.0.

surface.before:

export const PHAX_RELEASE = "0.20.0";

surface.after: $schema: "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/gate-diagnostics/<current stamp>.json"   never rewritten by the cut; a test fails while it differs from the format's current stamp

surface.before: Verify package versions match tag: npm/package.json and packages/schemas/package.json equal the tag
surface.after: Verify package versions match tag: npm/package.json, packages/schemas/package.json and the last entry of packages/schemas/releases.json equal the tag. A tag on an opening commit (manifests equal the tag, ledger ends earlier) fails here.

surface.surface: file: README.md, Extend phax, what `$schema` names
surface.before: `$schema` names the `gate-diagnostics` release the document is written for. A document without it fails the step, and so does one stamped with a release newer than the running phax.
surface.after: `$schema` names the `gate-diagnostics` shape the document is written in: the release that last changed the format. phax names the shape it reads whenever it refuses a document. A document without `$schema` fails the step, and so does one stamped newer than the running phax or in an older shape.

nonGoals: Pre-release suffixes (`-dev` and the like). The release workflow refuses them, and every `$schema` stays X.Y.Z.
Choosing the opened version automatically from commit messages.
Any change to how a released phax reads older releases. phax keeps reading `$schema` documents with its current decoder only, so it gains no frozen per-release decoders.
Reading documents that a development build stamped with an opened version later re-opened away (dev runs, scratch fixtures). They are unsupported, and nothing re-stamps them.
Re-stamping files already written. Files carrying the running-release stamps of 0.17.0–0.20.0 stay as they are and stay readable.
Changing which URLs the docs site serves for a ledger release. It keeps serving one URL per format per release.
Adding a field to any request or answer to carry the answer's stamp. No published format changes shape.
Reading older-shape answers through a frozen shape and lifting them. That is the 1.0 promise, not this change.
Re-deciding that stamps name the shape (decided 2026-10-08).

acceptanceCriteria.name: An unchanged format keeps its stamp across releases
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax whose running version is 0.21.0 and whose run-status shape last changed in 0.17.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: it writes a run's `run-status.json`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file's `$schema` is `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/run-status/0.17.0.json`

acceptanceCriteria.name: Requests carry their shape
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax at 0.21.0 with gate-request and brief-request unchanged since 0.20.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: it hands a gate step its request and a brief provider its request
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are stamped `gate-request/0.20.0` and `brief-request/0.20.0`, and the missing-document hint names `gate-diagnostics/0.20.0`

acceptanceCriteria.name: An unreleased change is stamped with the opened version, and the cut keeps it
acceptanceCriteria.given: a development build opened at 0.21.0 in which phase-status has a `next` snapshot
acceptanceCriteria.when: it writes a phase `status.json`, and the tree is then cut as 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file is stamped `phase-status/0.21.0` before the cut, and the cut build writes the same stamp

acceptanceCriteria.name: The schemas check holds phax's stamps to the snapshots
acceptanceCriteria.given: a tree where phax's current stamp for one format differs from its latest release-named snapshot (or from the opened version while `next` exists)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the schemas check runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: it fails and names that format

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax refuses a newer stamp
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: it reads a `phase-status/0.22.0` file, and then a gate step prints `gate-diagnostics/0.22.0`
acceptanceCriteria.then: both are refused as newer, naming 0.22.0 and 0.21.0

acceptanceCriteria.name: The package refuses a newer stamp
acceptanceCriteria.given: the schemas package at 0.20.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: it parses a phase-status stamped 0.22.0
acceptanceCriteria.then: it fails at `$schema`, naming 0.22.0 and the package's 0.20.0

acceptanceCriteria.name: An old consumer reads a newer phax's unchanged format
acceptanceCriteria.given: the schemas package at 0.20.0 and a phase-status phax 0.21.0 wrote while phase-status was unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.when: the package parses it
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reads it as shape 0.20.0

acceptanceCriteria.name: Running-release stamps from 0.18–0.20 stay readable
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `run-status.json` stamped `run-status/0.19.0` by phax 0.19.0 (shape 0.17.0)
acceptanceCriteria.when: a development build opened at 0.21.0 reads it, and the package at 0.21.0 parses it
acceptanceCriteria.then: phax reads it, and the package resolves it to shape 0.17.0

acceptanceCriteria.name: No fallback from next
acceptanceCriteria.given: the package opened at 0.21.0 with a `next` phase-status shape, and a document stamped 0.21.0 that only the 0.20.0 shape accepts
acceptanceCriteria.when: the package parses it
acceptanceCriteria.then: it fails with `next`'s violation and is never decoded as shape 0.20.0

acceptanceCriteria.name: Answers inside the window are read
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax at 0.21.0 with gate-diagnostics and brief-answer unchanged since 0.20.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: a gate step prints `gate-diagnostics/0.20.0`, and then `gate-diagnostics/0.21.0`
acceptanceCriteria.then: both are read. A brief answer stamped `brief-answer/0.21.0` is read too, and is read in the release built from the same tree

acceptanceCriteria.name: Older-shape answers are refused by name
acceptanceCriteria.given: a development build opened at 0.21.0 with a `next` gate-diagnostics shape
acceptanceCriteria.when: a gate step prints `gate-diagnostics/0.20.0`, and a brief provider answers `brief-answer/0.19.0`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first is refused as an older shape, naming `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/gate-diagnostics/0.21.0.json`; the second keeps its existing refusal

acceptanceCriteria.name: Refusals name the stamp phax reads
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax at 0.21.0 with brief-answer's current stamp 0.20.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: a gate step prints no document, and a brief provider answers without `$schema`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the step's failure names `gate-diagnostics/<current stamp>` and the brief refusal names `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/brief-answer/0.20.0.json`

acceptanceCriteria.name: A development build reads the installed release's run
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run folder written by phax 0.20.0 (registry, run-status, phase-status, phax-plan, all stamped 0.20.0)
acceptanceCriteria.when: a development build opened at 0.21.0 reads the registry and the run's status
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reads them with no refusal

acceptanceCriteria.name: A release refuses a development build's changed format
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax and the package at release 0.20.0, and a phase-status stamped 0.21.0 by a development build opened at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: each reads it
acceptanceCriteria.then: each refuses it as newer and does not decode it

acceptanceCriteria.name: The opened version is not a development build's pre-support stamp
acceptanceCriteria.given: the package opened at 0.21.0 with FIRST_SUPPORTED_RELEASE 0.17.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: it parses a document stamped 0.21.0, and one stamped 0.16.0
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first never gets the development-build message; the second still does

acceptanceCriteria.name: Releasing opens the next minor
acceptanceCriteria.given: main opened at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: `scripts/release.sh 0.21.0` completes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the commit after `chore: release v0.21.0` is `chore: open v0.22.0`, pushed. It sets the three manifests, `PHAX_RELEASE`, `PACKAGE_VERSION`, `phax.usage.kdl` and `docs/cli/reference.md` to 0.22.0, and leaves the ledger and snapshots unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.name: Re-opening by hand
acceptanceCriteria.given: a clean tree opened at 0.21.0 with a ledger ending at 0.20.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator runs `scripts/release.sh --open 0.22.0`, then `--open 0.20.0`, then `--open 0.22.0` again
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first commits an opening of 0.22.0. The second is refused as not newer than the last release, and the third as already opened. The refused runs write nothing

acceptanceCriteria.name: A failed opening names its remedy
acceptanceCriteria.given: a release whose tag was pushed and whose opening commit then fails
acceptanceCriteria.when: release.sh exits
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits non-zero and prints `scripts/release.sh --open <next minor>`

acceptanceCriteria.name: The cut refuses a version that was not opened
acceptanceCriteria.given: a copy of the tree opened at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: `release-cut.ts 0.22.0` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits non-zero, writes nothing, and names 0.21.0 and `scripts/release.sh --open 0.22.0`

acceptanceCriteria.name: The cut appends the opened version
acceptanceCriteria.given: a copy opened at 0.21.0 whose ledger ends at 0.20.0, and a second copy whose ledger already ends at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: `release-cut.ts 0.21.0` runs on each
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first ledger ends at 0.21.0; the second cut is refused and writes nothing

acceptanceCriteria.name: The cut is a rename and a ledger entry
acceptanceCriteria.given: a copy opened at 0.21.0 with a `next` phase-status snapshot
acceptanceCriteria.when: `release-cut.ts 0.21.0` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: `next.schema.json` becomes `0.21.0.schema.json`. The three manifests, `src/schemas/release.ts` and both hello-world scripts are byte-identical to before

acceptanceCriteria.name: Example stamps follow the format
acceptanceCriteria.given: a tree where gate-diagnostics gains a `next` snapshot and `audit.mjs` still prints `gate-diagnostics/0.20.0`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the unit tests run
acceptanceCriteria.then: a test fails, naming `examples/hello-world/audit.mjs` and the current stamp

acceptanceCriteria.name: The site serves only cut releases
acceptanceCriteria.given: main opened at 0.21.0 with a ledger ending at 0.20.0, and a made-up ledger listing 0.22.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: the site is built from each
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first passes and serves no `/schemas/*/0.21.0.json`; the second fails, naming the entry above package.json's version

acceptanceCriteria.name: A tag without a cut fails the workflow
acceptanceCriteria.given: `release.yml`
acceptanceCriteria.when: its version check runs on a commit whose manifests equal the tag but whose ledger ends at an earlier release
acceptanceCriteria.then: the step fails, and it runs before the docs deploy and the first stage publish

acceptanceCriteria.name: A development build reports the opened version
acceptanceCriteria.given: main opened at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax --version` runs from source and `phax.usage.kdl` and `docs/cli/reference.md` are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: all three report `0.21.0`, with no suffix

acceptanceCriteria.name: CI rehearses what will ship
acceptanceCriteria.given: `ci.yml`
acceptanceCriteria.when: its release rehearsal step runs on main opened at 0.21.0
acceptanceCriteria.then: it runs `scripts/release.sh --rehearse 0.21.0`, the version package.json names

acceptanceCriteria.name: The first cycle is opened
acceptanceCriteria.given: the change merged on main
acceptanceCriteria.when: the manifests, the generated files and the ledger are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the three manifests and `PHAX_RELEASE` name 0.21.0, and the ledger ends at 0.20.0. `docs/release.md` describes the opening, and the README describes stamps as shapes

openQuestions.question: Which version does release.sh open after a release?

options.label: Always the next minor (X.(Y+1).0)
options.abandons: Patch releases without a re-opening: a hotfix cycle, and after 1.0 any patch-only cycle, pays one `--open` commit.

options.label: Always the next patch (X.Y.(Z+1))
options.abandons: Matching how phax actually releases: every release since 0.17.0 has been a minor, so nearly every cycle would re-open.

options.label: Chosen by the operator at each release (a required argument)
options.abandons: A release that takes one decision: it asks the operator to predict the next cycle's size at the moment it starts.

openQuestions.rationale: It fits every release phax has cut since `$schema` existed. A wrong guess costs one `--open` commit, and the cut's refusal names that command.

openQuestions.question: What happens when the release to ship is not the opened version (0.21.0 opened, 0.21.1 or 0.22.0 wanted)?

options.label: The cut refuses; the operator re-opens with `--open`, then cuts
options.abandons: A one-command release when the cycle turned out bigger or smaller than opened: one more commit, and a CI round on it.

options.label: The cut accepts any version newer than the last release and re-stamps the manifests, the generated files and the examples
options.abandons: A rehearsed cut that renames no stamp: CI rehearsed the opened version, so the version actually cut was never rehearsed, and the cut takes back the manifest bump and the example rewrite this spec removes.

openQuestions.rationale: It keeps the invariant that matters: the version that ships is the one every commit of the cycle stamped and CI rehearsed. Either way, documents a development build stamped with the abandoned opened version are unsupported (non-goals). Re-opening makes that moment visible as a commit.

openQuestions.question: When does the release ledger gain a release?

options.label: At the cut, in the release commit (as today)
options.abandons: The invariant that the ledger ends at package.json's version on every commit. It holds only on release commits, so the site's check loosens to 'at or below', and the release workflow must check equality at the tag.

options.label: At the opening, so the ledger always ends at package.json's version
options.abandons: The ledger as a list of shipped releases: main's ledger names a version that may never ship, a re-opening rewrites it, and every main build of the site serves URLs for an unreleased version.

openQuestions.rationale: The ledger feeds the public schema URLs, and a served URL can never be withdrawn (the deploy guard refuses). It must name only what shipped. The looser site check is paid back by the tag-time ledger check, which also closes a hole: once manifests name the opened version, they alone would accept a tag on a commit that was never cut.

openQuestions.question: How does phax know each format's current stamp at run time, given that it never imports `packages/`?

options.label: A per-format table generated into `src/schemas/release.ts` from the snapshots, with `next` resolved to the opened version, and held by the schemas check
options.abandons: A single copy of the shape names: CURRENT_SHAPES and phax's table are two generated outputs of the same snapshots, kept equal by the check.

options.label: phax imports CURRENT_SHAPES from the package
options.abandons: The one-way dependency decided in q-historical-location (2026-10-01): phax would import `packages/`, which widens its TypeScript root and moves its build output.

options.label: Each schema module declares its format's stamp by hand
options.abandons: Snapshots as the one source of a shape's name: a contributor who changes a format must also remember to bump a literal, and nothing generated catches a missed bump.

openQuestions.rationale: The generator already writes `src/schemas/release.ts` from package.json and already reads the snapshots for CURRENT_SHAPES. One more generated fact keeps the dependency direction and the build unchanged, and the drift it adds is exactly what `schemas:check` exists to refuse.

openQuestions.question: How does a provider learn which stamp to answer in?

options.label: The README and the docs site document each format's shape, and every refusal or missing-document hint names the URL phax reads
options.abandons: A machine-readable answer at run time: a provider pins its answer stamp as a constant and learns a format changed when the new phax refuses it.

options.label: A new command (e.g. `phax schemas --json`) prints every format's current stamp
options.abandons: A smaller CLI surface before the 1.0 freeze: one more command and output format to hold, built for consumers whose constants now break only when a format changes.

options.label: phax passes the expected answer URL in the provider's environment
options.abandons: A contract carried by the documents alone: a second, unversioned channel beside the request, outside every published schema.

openQuestions.rationale: With shape stamps a pinned constant breaks only when the format it names changes, which is when the provider must change its code anyway. The refusal that names the expected URL is the signal it needs then, and it adds no surface.

openQuestions.question: Does a development build mark its version as unreleased?

options.label: No: `phax --version`, the usage spec and the CLI reference print the bare opened version
options.abandons: Telling a development build from a release at a glance: a contributor's bug report says 0.21.0 before 0.21.0 exists.

options.label: Yes: `--version` prints e.g. `0.21.0 (unreleased)` in a development build
options.abandons: One version string: it needs a third generated fact that the cut sets and the opening clears, and `--version` stops matching the usage spec generated from the same tree.

openQuestions.rationale: npm and GitHub Releases carry only tagged builds, so an opened version reaches only contributors running from source, where `git describe` already says whether the build is a release. The marker would cost a moving part in the cut for a reader who already has the answer.

settled: Stamps name the format's shape (author, 2026-10-08). This amends the archived schemas-package spec's q-release-name (Q16). The archive stays as written, and `docs/release.md` records the new rule.
Shape stamps resolve `next` to the opened version, so a cut never changes a stamp. It renames `next` snapshots and appends the ledger; the manifests were bumped by the opening.

The newer refusal compares the stamp to the reader's running version, not to the format's shape, because files that 0.17.0–0.20.0 wrote carry running-release stamps above their format's shape (e.g. run-status/0.20.0 over shape 0.17.0).
The package's `defineFormat` drops the fallback from `next` to a released shape for a stamp at its own version. The 'latest shape at or below the stamp' rule otherwise stays.
The answer readers drop their exception for the running release. Their lower bound becomes the format's current stamp. Stamps at or below 0.19.0 keep their existing refusals.
Before 1.0, older-shape answers are refused by name (author, 2026-10-08). The guard tests that hold each answer reader to one shape must, at 1.0, fail and name that rule rather than be deleted.
FIRST_SUPPORTED_RELEASE and the development-build message are unchanged.

Recommended defaults, pending §9: open the next minor, refuse a cut of any version other than the opened one, the ledger gains a release at its cut, a generated stamp table in `src/schemas/release.ts`, providers learn their stamp from the docs and from refusals, and the version stays bare.
open: The spelling of `--open`, of the stamp table, and of the refusal and hint messages.
Whether the opening commit runs any tests before it is pushed, and whether `--open` also pushes or only commits.
Whether docs-deploy.yml gets the same ledger-equals-tag check as release.yml.
Whether the README's stamped examples (gate-diagnostics, gate-request, brief-request, brief-answer) join the example-stamp test or stay hand-held.
Whether `LAST_SAVED_FILE_ONLY_DIAGNOSTICS_RELEASE` and `LAST_RELEASE_WITHOUT_BRIEF_ANSWER` stay as named constants once the current stamp bounds the answers from below.
constraints: No back-compat shims in persisted schemas, and no change to any published format's shape.
Every `$schema` stays `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/<format id>/<X.Y.Z>.json`, with no suffix.
Files the installed release wrote stay readable by a development build.
Neither the docs site nor the release workflow serves or publishes the opened version; served URLs are never withdrawn.
Docs to update: `docs/release.md` (opening, `--open`, the cut, the rehearsal, the workflow's ledger check), the README's Extend phax section, and the `phax-cli` skill if it quotes stamps.

Tests to update: `tests/unit/releaseCut.test.ts`, `tests/unit/releaseWorkflow.test.ts`, `tests/unit/site/schemas.test.ts`, `tests/unit/schemasPackage/` (the fallback, CURRENT_SHAPES parity), the answer-reader and bridge tests, and every fixture that stamps `PHAX_RELEASE` where it means a format's shape.

docsPage.page: README §Extend phax (rendered on docs.phax.run), with what `$schema` names; `docs/release.md` for maintainers
docsPage.reader: The author of a gate step or brief provider (steme first), deciding which `$schema` to print and when to update it; and the maintainer cutting a release.
docsPage.example: phax 0.21.0 sends `gate-request/0.20.0.json` and reads `gate-diagnostics/0.20.0.json` for as long as neither format changes, so a step that prints `gate-diagnostics/0.20.0` keeps working across phax releases. When a release changes gate-diagnostics, phax refuses the old stamp and names the URL it now reads. Maintainers: `scripts/release.sh 0.21.0` cuts the version main already names, then opens 0.22.0.
